item.title: Delta govt approves N4bn to empower 1500 indigenes
item.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi & Ochuko Akuopha The Delta State Government has approved N4 billion to empower 15,000 indigent residents to support small businesses and entrepreneurship. The initiative is part of efforts to ease economic hardship across the state. The State Commissioner for Works (Rural Roads) and Public Information, Mr Charles Aniagwu, disclosed this while briefing journalists after the State Executive Council meeting presided over by Governor Sheriff Oborevwori at Government House, Asaba. The Commissioner who was accompanied by the Chief Press Secretary to the Governor, Sir Festus Ahon, said beneficiaries will be drawn from the 25 local government areas under an initiative designed to improve livelihoods and strengthen the purchasing power of vulnerable residents. Aniagwu said the intervention would be implemented through the Delta State Social Investment Programme in the coming weeks, adding that the governor had directed that the selection process be guided by clear eligibility criteria. According to him, priority will be given to indigent persons who already operate small businesses, those seeking to establish micro-enterprises and vulnerable residents who require financial support to improve their circumstances. He said the grant was intended to help existing businesses overcome economic challenges, provide start-up capital for aspiring entrepreneurs and enable beneficiaries to meet pressing needs. The commissioner explained that the initiative was part of the government’s efforts to ensure that the benefits of ongoing economic reforms translated into tangible improvements in the lives of ordinary Deltans. item.title: Kompany hospitalised after collapsing at Bayern training ground
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany has reportedly been taken to hospital after collapsing at the club’s training ground on Friday, amid concerns over a viral infection that has affected his health in recent days. According to Sky Sports Germany, the 40-year-old Belgian received medical attention before being taken by ambulance to a hospital in Munich. A rescue helicopter was also seen landing at Bayern’s training complex at Säbener Straße. Reports said Kompany had been battling a viral infection that caused significant discomfort, including problems with his legs and difficulties climbing stairs. German newspaper Bild also reported that the illness had aggravated problems involving old scar tissue. The former Manchester City captain had experienced health concerns before Bayern’s 6-1 Bundesliga victory over RB Leipzig last weekend, when he reportedly spent periods of the match seated in the dugout. He subsequently missed training and the pre-match press conference ahead of Bayern’s Champions League meeting with Arsenal on Wednesday, leaving assistant coach Aaron Danks to address the media. Danks said Kompany had been advised to rest while recovering, although he acknowledged that persuading the manager to take time away from his duties was difficult. “Getting Vince to rest is a challenge,” Danks said. Kompany recovered sufficiently to take charge of Bayern’s 2-2 draw with Arsenal at the Allianz Arena. After the match, he admitted that he had continued working despite the illness. “I caught a pretty nasty virus last week, and of course I didn’t listen to my body,” he said. The latest reports said Kompany was in a stable condition, although the precise circumstances surrounding the reported collapse remained unclear. Bayern had not issued a detailed official medical update at the time of reporting. The German champions are scheduled to face Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday, with Kompany’s availability for the fixture uncertain. Assistant coach Danks could take charge if the Belgian requires further time to recover. The post Kompany hospitalised after collapsing at Bayern training ground appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu’s 90-day relief plan a scam to bait voters — ADC campaign
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike The African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council has accused President Bola Tinubu of using his 90-day cost-of-living relief plan to bait voters ahead of the 2027 presidential election, arguing that the programme’s deadline falls after Nigerians would have voted. Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, said the timing of the plan raised questions about the administration’s commitment to easing hardship after three and a half years of rising living costs, insisting that Nigerians should judge the President by his record rather than another promise of relief. Addressing a press conference at the ADC Secretariat on Friday, Shaibu said the government’s proposed intervention amounted to an election tactic, given that the presidential election was 86 days away while the relief plan would run for 90 days. “The arithmetic is plain: the plan ends after Nigerians have voted. After three and a half years of hardship, this government is asking families to carry another promise into the polling booth and wait for relief until the votes are counted,” Shaibu added. He said the plan’s five priorities; food affordability, tax harmonisation, completion of major projects, removal of investment bottlenecks and household support were problems Nigerians had expected the government to address long before the election approached. Shaibu argued that the removal of petrol subsidy had driven up transport, food and production costs, while adequate protection for vulnerable households had not accompanied the policy. “A government cannot put a 90-day deadline on hunger, the cost-of-living crisis and insecurity and call it an economic policy,” he said. The ADC campaign council also questioned the effectiveness of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited’s petrol discount promotion, which began on October 1 and was presented as part of the government’s relief effort. Shaibu said he visited NNPC Retail stations to assess the promotion and claimed that attendants told him no discount was available. He said he bought petrol at ₦1,405 per litre. “With barely a week left before the offer expires, my experience as a customer was simple: a promise of relief, and a higher price at the pump,” he said. He challenged NNPC to publish the number of customers who benefited, the stations where the discount was available and the volume of petrol sold at the reduced price. With NNPC operating about 900 retail stations nationwide, Shaibu questioned the reach of a ₦66-per-litre discount in a country where motorists buy fuel from thousands of outlets, adding that the offer did little to address persistently high transport and food costs. The opposition spokesman also raised concerns about a registration form circulating under the name “Arise for Tinubu 2027”, which he said requested voter identification, bank details and telephone numbers. “Who is collecting this sensitive personal information, how will it be used, and is the exercise connected to the household support the government has announced?” he asked. Shaibu demanded clarification on whether the registration exercise was linked to any publicly funded relief programme, warning that Nigerians should not have to surrender voter or bank details to a political group to access public assistance. The ADC campaign council also questioned Tinubu’s record on security and his response to civilian casualties and disasters in Kaduna State, where the President is expected to launch his re-election campaign. Shaibu recalled the December 3, 2023, military drone strike on civilians attending a Maulud celebration in Tudun Biri, in which at least 85 people were killed, and criticised Tinubu for not personally visiting the community after the tragedy. He also cited reported civilian deaths in a September 2024 military airstrike in Giwa, abductions in Kajuru and a September 2025 kidnapping-related attack in Kachia, alongside storms and flooding that affected communities across Kaduna State. “Tinubu can find his way to Kaduna for a wedding. He can find his way there for votes. Why was he absent when grieving families needed their President?” Shaibu asked. He urged the President to explain what had been done for victims of the Tudun Biri strike, the outcome of investigations into civilian deaths and the measures being taken to protect communities still threatened by abductions. Returning to the economic plan, Shaibu demanded specific details on how the government intended to reduce food prices, harmonise taxes, complete projects, ease constraints on businesses and deliver household support within 90 days. He said the administration should publish the eligibility criteria, budget, payment arrangements and duration of the proposed household assistance, as well as identify the projects expected to be completed within the period. The ADC campaign spokesman said Nigerians had endured the burden of the government’s economic reforms and deserved evidence that the promised benefits would reach them and remain in place beyond election day. “People do not reject reform because they fail to understand it. They reject being told to sacrifice today for relief that never arrives, or arrives with an expiry date,” he said. Shaibu said ADC presidential hopeful Atiku Abubakar had pledged to make Nigeria affordable through disciplined public spending, targeted household relief, lower production and transportation costs, and policies to help manufacturers expand and create jobs. He challenged Tinubu to explain whether Nigerians were better off than they were in May 2023 and whether the promised relief would remain meaningful after the 90-day period. “Tinubu must answer two questions: Are Nigerians better off than they were in May 2023? And will they still be able to afford food on day 91 of his plan?” Shaibu asked. He maintained that the proposed programme risked becoming a political timetable dressed up as economic relief, urging Nigerians not to exchange their experience of three and a half years of hardship for promises timed around the election. item.title: Eko Power assures solar users of no penalties
item.description: Eko Power Ltd. says customers who invest in solar energy will not be penalised or disconnected for low electricity consumption. Mr Abiola Aloba, General Manager, Corporate Communication Unit of Eko Power, said this in a statement on Friday in Lagos. The company’s clarification followed a complaint by Mr Raphael Awoseyin on Oct. 19, alleging repeated visits by its personnel after installing an 18-kilowatt solar power system at his property. Awoseyin said that the personnel inspected his prepaid meter over suspicions of meter bypass because it was recording little or no electricity consumption. He also alleged that the company issued him a disconnection notice and demanded N112,606 as a loss-of-revenue charge. Aloba, however, said that the company had cancelled the charge in full and withdrawn the disconnection notice, adding that Awoseyin had never been disconnected. “The ‘Loss of Revenue’ demand has been cancelled in full. It should not have been made, and the customer doesn’t owe us,” he said. Aloba said Eko Power supported customers investing in alternative energy sources and would not penalise them for reducing their dependence on the national grid. “Eko Power supports customers who invest in solar. Low electricity consumption is not a reason to disconnect anyone,” he said. He explained that the customer’s prepaid meter, which had been in service for many years, was found to be faulty during testing. According to him, the company replaced the meter at no cost to the customer and would not impose back-billing, reconciliation charges or other costs arising from the incident. Awoseyin said that he relied mainly on solar energy during the day and used electricity supplied by Eko Power as backup at night. He explained that he briefly switched to the company’s electricity supply to demonstrate that his meter could record consumption. According to him, the meter recorded consumption during the demonstration, but the company’s personnel returned the following day with a disconnection notice. Awoseyin said his last electricity token purchase was in July 2026 and that he still had some units remaining. He alleged that the personnel attributed the low consumption to a faulty meter and demanded N112,606 to recover the company’s alleged revenue loss. Awoseyin said he offered to have the meter tested but was told that the company needed to recover the amount because it was losing revenue. item.title: 1 die, 3 injured in alleged attack on NDC candidate’s convoy in Ebonyi
item.description: The Police in Ebonyi have confirmed one person dead and three others injured following an alleged attack on the convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) House of Assembly candidate. The Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), SP Joshua Ukandu, confirmed this on Friday in Abakaliki with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN). Ukandu said the incident occurred at about 4 p.m. on Thursday at Amaezekwe community in Ezza South Local Government Area of the state. The PPRO said the command received a distress call reporting a disturbance in the community and immediately dispatched operatives to the scene. “Upon arrival, the operatives found four individuals with gunshot wounds and a burnt vehicle. “One of the victims was confirmed dead at the hospital, while the three others are receiving medical treatment,” he said. Meanwhile, the NDC candidate for Ezza South Constituency in the state, Mr Offia-Nwali, said suspected political thugs attacked his motorcade and set his Toyota Hilux vehicle ablaze. In a statement issued to newsmen in Abakaliki, Offia-Nwali said he and members of his entourage escaped unhurt during the incident. He expressed sympathy with those affected by the attack and urged youths in the state not to allow themselves to be used by politicians to pursue personal ambitions. “No political ambition is worth the life of any young person,” he said. item.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Delta Governorship Candidate Mr Chris Iyovwaye, has pledged to drive industrialisation as vehicle for job creation and sustainable development in the state if elected in 2027. Iyovwaye made the pledge during a consultation with Chief Emmanuel Nwachukwu, Managing Director, Benco Pools, and his grassroots movement on Friday in Agbor, Ika South Local Government Area of Delta. The NDC delegation, led by Iyovwaye, includes the party’s Delta North senatorial candidate, Mr Victor Ochei, and other candidates from Ika Federal Constituency. Others were the party’s candidates for Ika North-East Constituency I, Mr Sylvester Chukwuedo, and Ika South Constituency, Mrs Ogor Tony-Obuh. Iyovwaye criticised poor management of Delta’s common patrimony and the lack of innovative leadership capable of translating resources into tangible benefits. He said industrialisation would drive economic growth, create employment and promote sustainable development if supported by practical policies and measurable results. The governorship candidate said the NDC remained committed to changing the state’s development trajectory through policies that would unlock its economic potentials. Iyovwaye also expressed confidence in the quality of the party’s candidates across all levels, including its presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi. He called for the support of Nwachukwu and his associates, saying Delta has greater economic potential than the reflected current level of development. Also, Ochei thanked Nwachukwu for receiving the delegation and recalled his earlier visit to the business leader a few days before the consultation. He described the developing relationship as a partnership with the potential to benefit all parties, particularly the people. The other candidates outlined their commitment to effective representation and development and reinforced the delegation’s message of coordinated engagement across Ika Federal Constituency and Delta North. The party’s Delta North Senatorial Chairman, Mr Aaron Ebenuwa, also led members of the party leadership on the visit. item.title: Terrorism: FG secures 653 convictions, prosecutes 1,060 suspects
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Federal Government has secured a total of 653 convictions of persons arrested across the federation for their involvement in various acts of terrorism. The convicts, some of whom were found guilty of aiding insurgents or concealing information about their operations from security agencies, were among the 1,060 persons brought before the court in the third phase of the ongoing mass trial of terror suspects. Speaking to newsmen shortly after stepping out of the courtroom on Friday, the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, who led the prosecution, disclosed that a total of 880 cases had been heard, out of which the court convicted 653, acquitted seven and discharged 27 of the defendants. He said the exercise would continue and the final figures would be announced after the conclusion of the trial. Describing the current phase of the mass trial as the largest since the FG commenced the special court sessions for the prosecution of terror suspects, the AGF attributed the success of the exercise to judicial cooperation, effective prosecution and inter-agency collaboration. He expressed appreciation to the judges handling the cases, particularly Justice Binta Nyako, who has been acting on behalf of the Chief Judge of the Federal High Court, Justice John Tsoho. The AGF also commended the prosecution team, the defence counsel and the security agencies for contributing to the smooth conduct of the proceedings. Among the agencies he acknowledged for their contributions were the Office of the National Security Adviser (NSA), the Department of State Services (DSS), the military, the police, correctional centres and the Legal Aid Council of Nigeria (LACoN). According to the AGF, collaboration among the institutions has been critical to advancing the prosecution of terrorism, terrorism financing and related offences in the country. On the representation of the defendants by lawyers from the LACoN, the AGF explained that the council was fulfilling its responsibility of providing legal assistance to eligible defendants. He clarified, however, that private legal practitioners were also representing some of the suspects. He said the defence lawyers were not only given the opportunity to interact with their clients before the court proceedings, but were also granted access to the detention facilities to enable them to prepare the defendants’ defence effectively. On the issue of deradicalisation of suspects recommended by the court, the AGF said the process remained an important component of the overall exercise. He maintained that rehabilitation and reintegration were necessary to complement the judicial process and reduce the risk of individuals returning to extremist activities. item.description: The Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, has met the threshold of two-thirds of the 36 state Houses of Assembly as required by law, the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill said on Friday. Chairman of the group and Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, disclosed in a statement that the bill has been approved by 24 Houses of Assembly. “The Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill notes with satisfaction that the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, providing for a dual policing system, has been approved by 24 State Houses of Assembly, meeting the constitutional threshold of two-thirds of the 36 states,” it said. “The Working Group commends the State Houses of Assembly for their decisive action on this reform of national importance and appreciates the National Assembly for passing the amendment in both chambers.” Members of the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill: (L-R) Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun; Gbajabiamila; Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi; and Inspector General of Police, Olatunji Disu, addressing journalists on August 3, 2026. item.title: Tinubu condoles family of Nollywood veteran, Francis Duru‎‎
item.description: ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru President Bola Tinubu has expressed sorrow over the death of veteran Nollywood actor, Richard Francis Duru, extending his heartfelt condolences to his family, colleagues, fans and the Nigerian film industry. item.title: Bruno Fernandes’ home burgled during Man Utd’s 4-1 defeat to Como
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes’ home was burgled while the midfielder was in Italy with his team for their 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como on Wednesday, with police investigating the incident. According to ESPN, Fernandes’ family were not believed to have been at the property when the burglary occurred on Wednesday, October 21. Police attended the scene and Manchester United are supporting their captain. A statement from Cheshire Police, given to ESPN, said officers were called at about 8.30 pm to reports of suspicious activity at an address in the Alderley Park area of Nether Alderley. “The caller reported three unknown men in the rear garden of a neighbouring property,” the statement said. Officers found no trace of the suspects when they arrived but discovered that a burglary had taken place and a number of items had been stolen. “An investigation into the incident has been launched and enquiries are ongoing,” police added. Detective Inspector David Jarvis of Macclesfield Proactive CID said the investigation was at an early stage, adding that officers were working to identify those responsible. Police have appealed to anyone who was in the area at the time and may have witnessed suspicious activity to come forward. They also urged residents with relevant CCTV or dashcam footage to assist the investigation. The burglary came as United endured a difficult spell on the pitch, with their 4-1 defeat to Como extending their winless run to seven matches in all competitions. Fernandes publicly questioned the tactical approach of head coach Michael Carrick after the Champions League loss, saying the decision not to press opponents man-to-man and to leave space behind was a matter for the coaching staff. His comments followed criticism from United defender Lisandro Martínez the previous week, adding to scrutiny of the club’s leadership and performances. Despite the heavy defeat and questions over Carrick’s future, the United manager is expected to remain in charge for Sunday’s Premier League match against Bournemouth, ESPN reported. Fernandes, who was one of United’s standout performers last season, has struggled to reproduce the same form this campaign as the club faces growing pressure to improve its results. item.title: 2027: Wike debunks viral post backing Adamawa LP candidate, Abbo
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has debunked a social media post claiming he is backing Senator Ishaku Abbo, the Labour Party LP candidate in next year’s Adamawa State governorship election. Wike, who spoke through his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media, Lere Olayinka, described the report as fake. Olayinka said the minister has no relationship with the LP or any of its candidates in Adamawa State. The post in question quoted Wike as urging the people of Adamawa State to make informed and thoughtful decisions at the ballot, adding that, in his opinion, Abbo is best fit to lead the state. The minister, however, said he did not at any time endorse Abbo or any other LP candidate. He urged the people of Adamawa State to disregard the post, stressing that whoever he is supporting, he will say so with his own mouth. item.title: The pressure before the click: How I decide whether a setup deserves capital
item.description: By Kojo Forex, Exness Team Pro Trader Many traders assume pressure begins after a position is open. When do I feel the most pressure? In the few moments before I’ve decided on a trade. The pressure makes you ask yourself: Am I doing the right thing? Have I ticked every box? Am I convinced enough? That small window matters because once the order is placed, the decision is exposed. The market can move in favor of the setup or against it, but I no longer have the freedom to rewrite the plan. For me, control starts before that point. Putting numbers behind the decision Conviction alone is not enough. Before committing my capital, I want to understand what the trade requires from the account. That means looking beyond the setup’s direction and considering the position size, margin, and potential trading costs. When I trade using Exness Terminal, the trading calculator lets me estimate values such as required margin, spread cost, commission, and swap for a planned position. It gives me concrete information to consider before I place the order. The calculator doesn’t decide whether a setup is good, and it doesn’t remove the risk. The judgement remains mine, but its value is that it helps me put numbers behind the decision before pressure or momentum can take over. That is the role I want technology to play: making the trade-offs visible without making the decision for me. The candle-close decision I enter most of my trades around candle closures, especially within the one-hour timeframe. That creates a specific kind of pressure. A setup may look close to confirmation, price may begin moving away from the zone, and the candle may still have a few minutes left before it closes. I think of it as distance against time. If a market usually covers a move in five or six candles but now needs many more candles to reach the same area, that tells me something. item.title: 2027: Tinubu’s aide claims CityBoy Movement has support across party lines
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Senior Special Assistant to President Bola Tinubu on Digital/New Media, O’tega Ogra, has claimed that the CityBoy Movement has been welcomed by a majority of Nigerian youths and has attracted members across party lines, including from opposition parties, ahead of the 2027 general election. Ogra, who is also Deputy Director-General of the CityBoy Movement, a group campaigning in support of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, made the claim on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday while responding to questions about the movement’s reach and acceptance among young Nigerians. When asked about areas where the movement had yet to gain acceptance, Ogra said he was open to discussing any such areas but maintained that the movement had received support from a majority of Nigerian youths. “I mean, if you show me one, I might be able to speak to that. But as far as I know, we have been welcomed by a majority of Nigerian youths,” he said. Ogra also claimed that the movement had members across the political divide, including people associated with major opposition parties. “We’re a movement that has members across the political space. We have members from the PDP. We have members from Alhaji Atiku’s own party. We have members that have come from Peter Obi’s own party. We have members who belong to Seyi Makinde’s government within our structure,” he said. Explaining what he believed was driving the movement’s appeal among young Nigerians, Ogra said youths were tired of political leaders who, in his view, made promises they failed to keep and diverted public funds for private interests. “Because at the end of the day, the Nigerian youths, we are done with people telling us lies. We are done with people promising one thing and putting government funds into their private enterprise,” he said. He further argued that young Nigerians were better equipped to scrutinise political leaders because of their access to information and fact-checking tools. “We’re done with people, you know, trying to play on our intelligence. We are smarter than whatever was in the 1990s or in the 2000s. We have access to news, we have access to information, we can fact check, we can revalidate, we have these things at our fingertips and one thing that we have chosen to do at the City Boy movement, our motto is inform, engage, empower,” Ogra added. We have members who belong to Seyi Makinde’s government within our structure,” he said. Explaining what he believed was driving the movement’s appeal among young Nigerians, Ogra said youths were tired of political leaders who, in his view, made promises they failed to keep and diverted public funds for private interests. “Because at the end of the day, the Nigerian youths, we are done with people telling us lies. We are done with people promising one thing and putting government funds into their private enterprise,” he said. He further argued that young Nigerians were better equipped to scrutinise political leaders because of their access to information and fact-checking tools. “We’re done with people, you know, trying to play on our intelligence. We are smarter than whatever was in the 1990s or in the 2000s. We have access to news, we have access to information, we can fact check, we can revalidate, we have these things at our fingertips and one thing that we have chosen to do at the City Boy movement, our motto is inform, engage, empower,” Ogra added. item.title: Shun partisan politics, Aiyedatiwa tells Ondo corps members
item.description: By Dayo Johnson Akure Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo State has charged members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) deployed to the state to avoid partisan politics in their host communities. Aiyedatiwa gave the charge at the closing ceremony and terminal parade of the 2026 Batch C Stream I orientation course held at Ikare-Akoko. Represented by the State Coordinator of the scheme, Mrs Kuburat Omowumi Bakare, the governor urged the corps members to be conscious of their responsibilities. “Remain mindful of the responsibilities that come with your position as corps members. Your actions will reflect not only on you but also on your families, your institutions and the NYSC,” he said. He appealed to employers and heads of establishments to receive corps members posted to them with cooperation and understanding. “Provide them with a conducive working environment, appropriate guidance and opportunities to contribute their knowledge and skills. Your mentorship can help them grow professionally and gain valuable experience that will serve them well beyond their service year,” Aiyedatiwa said. He also called on local government authorities, traditional rulers and community leaders to support corps members in their areas to aid their integration and effective execution of Community Development Service projects. “Your cooperation is essential to their successful integration into host communities and to the effective implementation of Community Development Service projects. By working together, we can ensure that the presence of corps members translates into tangible benefits for the people of Ondo State,” he added. The governor further urged the corps members to accept their postings in good faith and serve with diligence, integrity and respect for their host communities. “Approach your responsibilities with a strong sense of duty. Accept your postings in good faith and serve with diligence, integrity and respect for the people among whom you will live and work. Be willing to learn from your host communities, respect their customs and cultural values and conduct yourselves in ways that will earn their trust and confidence. “Your service year should be about more than fulfilling an obligation. It should be an opportunity to contribute meaningfully to society,” he said. Aiyedatiwa assured that his administration will continue to collaborate with security agencies and other stakeholders to ensure a safe environment for corps members throughout the service year. He cautioned them against compromising their personal security, advising them to remain vigilant, avoid late-night movements and unsafe gatherings, and shun unsolicited rides from strangers. “Be cautious when visiting unfamiliar or isolated places and promptly report suspicious activities or security concerns to the appropriate authorities. “Shun drug abuse, cybercrime, fraud and other unlawful activities that could jeopardise your future and bring disrepute to the scheme,” the governor added.
